A fisherman's anchor got stuck on a giant pearl, worth $100M during a storm in Palawan island, Philippines. Man took it home thinking it was a rock and a good luck charm, and was there in his house for 10 years. When his house caught on fire, he took this to a local tourism office.

This massive object is often described as the “Pearl of Puerto” or the “Palawan Pearl,” discovered off the coast of Palawan in the Philippines.

According to reports, a local fisherman found it around 2006 when his boat anchor snagged on something heavy during a storm. He kept the 34-kilogram (about 75-pound) object under his bed for nearly a decade, believing it was simply a large stone and a good luck charm. In 2016, after a fire damaged his home, he brought it to local authorities, where it was identified as a giant natural clam pearl.

If authenticated and valued at the figures sometimes cited, up to $100 million, it would surpass the famous “Pearl of Lao Tzu” (formerly the Pearl of Allah), long considered the largest known pearl.

However, its exact valuation remains debated, as giant clam “pearls” differ from traditional nacreous pearls found in oysters and are difficult to price on the conventional gemstone market.

The pearl reportedly came from a giant clam (Tridacna gigas), a species that can weigh over 400 pounds and live more than 100 years in the wild. When the fisherman brought the 34-kilogram (75-pound) object to authorities in 2016, it was turned over to the local government of Puerto Princesa City in Palawan. The city placed it on public display as a tourism attraction rather than selling it.  As far as the fisherman, local officials publicly praised the fisherman for turning it in, but there is no confirmed report that he was paid anything close to the rumored value. Some sources suggest he may have received modest assistance, but not even close to the value of the pearl.

© Reddit

#archaeohistories
